## The problem

Describe the situation you are in, not the solution you have in mind. "Every
project I start needs X and I rebuild it by hand each time" is far more useful
than "add X".

## Why it belongs in a minimal template

<!--
This project is deliberately small: it is a starting point, and every addition
is weight that every downstream app carries. Make the case that this is
something most cross-platform desktop apps need, rather than something specific
to one product.

Strong arguments look like:
- it demonstrates a practice that is easy to get subtly wrong
- it closes a correctness or security gap present in the current template
- it removes more code than it adds
-->

## What it would touch

- [ ] Frontend (`src/`)
- [ ] Rust backend (`src-tauri/`)
- [ ] Tooling / scripts (`scripts/`)
- [ ] CI (`.github/workflows/`)
- [ ] Documentation only
- [ ] New dependency <!-- name it, and say why a hand-rolled version is worse -->
